- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently low (sentiment < 0.3) — add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag in early days of the 30-day horizon — adjust upward by 1–3% for the first 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves — cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day high if sentiment is high.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.8), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5 day moving average.
- If sentiment is 1.0 for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should not exceed 10% above recent 14-day high — avoid overconfidence bias.
